neighbours.label: The preposition introducing the activity complement of a reason or motive noun ('the reason one has for acting', 'her motive for leaving'), vs the same nouns without an activity complement
fire: Nobody could understand the motive she had for selling the farm so quickly.
His only excuse for missing the meeting was a flat tyre.
Curiosity is the main reason many students have for studying astronomy.
The police are still looking for a motive for setting the fire.
Money was never her reason for taking the job at the hospital.
The coach gave a clear justification for benching the captain.
Boredom was the reason the boys gave for climbing onto the roof.
Fear of failure is a common reason people have for avoiding new hobbies.
quiet: Nobody could understand the motive behind the sudden sale of the farm.
His excuse was a flat tyre on the way to the meeting.
Curiosity is the main reason many students enjoy astronomy.
The police are still looking for a motive in the fire case.
Money was never the reason she stayed at the hospital.
The coach gave a clear explanation after the match.
Boredom was the reason, according to the boys on the roof.
Fear of failure is a common reason that people stay at home.

predictions: 'for' after reason/motive/excuse + gerund 0.2-0.45; the same nouns followed by 'was', 'that' or a location under 0.05.
notes: Card: peaks ' to' x9, ',', ' of', ' for' in 'purpose of research', 'reason one has for acting', 'favorite role to dance', 'like to make'. Probe: 'the reason a person has for working hard' 0.434 was the only strong item; 'left the office to pick up' 0.140, 'like to build' 0.082, 'favorite song to sing' 0.033, 'purpose of teaching' 0.029. The test bets on the reason/motive + for + activity frame; expect a fail if the probe's one hit does not generalize.
